 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti escalated his criticism of the College Football Playoff rankings Monday, this time using his team's only loss as evidence in Indiana's favor.
 The defending national champions are 9-1 but were ranked No. 9 in the second CFP rankings released last week, dropping five spots during their Week 10 bye.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Cignetti went on a three-minute rant defending his team against critics claiming Indiana hasn't played strong opponents.
 "Well, you know, we don't play anybody," Cignetti said sarcastically. "We have a soft schedule, right? That's all I've heard around here for three years because people love to discredit us and what we've accomplished.
 "We played Northwestern. They were undefeated. I knew they were a good team. It was a tough game. (…) Went out to Nebraska. They're 5-0. They got an 11-point lead on us in the fourth quarter. We come back and win."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Cignetti then pointed directly to Indiana's 19-15 loss to Ohio State, arguing the result changed the Buckeyes' season entirely.
 "Ohio State, who everybody picked to win the national championship this year. Both- we're 5-0, they're 5-1. You saw what happened," Cignetti said. "We knocked the quarterback out. We ripped the heart out of that team. They haven't been the same since without the quarterback. But all I hear about is how we lost to a three-loss team."
 Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin suffered a shoulder injury in that game and hasn't played after that. The Buckeyes have gone 1-2 since, and are 7-3 through 10 games.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti© Kyle Robertson/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images
 "That was a team picked to win a national championship that led Texas 95 percent of the game at Texas," Cignetti said. "We missed a layup. You know what? They won; we didn't. But we missed a layup. That's why we're not 26-0; we're 25-1."
 Cignetti's comments continued a weeks-long pattern. After the first CFP rankings, Cignetti accused ESPN of giving the SEC favorable treatment. After Indiana fell from No. 4 to No. 9 without playing, he posted , "Bad losses don't count anymore? Are first downs still 10 yards?"
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After beating No. 18 USC 27-13 last weekend, Cignetti bluntly challenged the narrative around Indiana's résumé, next facing the Washington Huskies at 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday.
 "I'm 65 years old, and I really don't give a (expletive)," Cignetti said.
